summary: Ran the agent-server type-check and test suite, which surfaced 18 failing tests across extension resource discovery, run-script workspace validation, Pi runtime config file permissions, and session repository isolation. Verified protocol schemas, then smoke-tested the live WebSocket agent at ws://127.0.0.1:8787/agent — session.create succeeded when integrations was passed as an empty array but failed with "Integration root must be inside the workspace" when omitted, exposing a path validation issue in pi-agent-service.
decisions: Committed the prior batch of Pi-runtime web-mode changes as `feat: use default Pi runtime resources in web mode` (commit 0328dac), covering pi-runtime-config, pi-agent-service, the matching test, vite-env.d.ts, README, docs/resources.md, docs/extensions.md, package.json, and pnpm-lock.yaml.

Verified the protocol's sessionOptionsSchema (packages/protocol/src/index.ts line 56) requires cwd, integrations, and domainId as optional fields with additionalProperties=false, so omitting integrations is what triggers the integration-root validation error path.
errors: pnpm test reported 18 failing tests; extension-resources.test.ts (5/8), run-script.test.ts (9/10), pi-runtime-config.test.ts (2/4), session-repository.test.ts (1/1), and discover-resources.test.ts (1/3).
packageResourceRoots/extensionResourceRoots returned `{ skills: [], prompts: [] }` instead of the expected temp-directory paths, indicating resource roots are not being populated.

runScript consistently threw "Script must be inside the workspace: <file>" for build.ts, run.ts, fail.ts, slow.ts, loud.ts, flood.ts, install.sh, missing.ts — the workspace-path guard rejects paths before shell-type, missing-bun, missing-script, and output-handling branches run, so downstream assertions never execute.
pi-runtime-config.test.ts file-permission assertion got mode 438 (0o666) instead of expected 384 (0o600) for auth.json, meaning the imported config is not being chmod-restricted.

WebSocket smoke `session.create` without `integrations` returned `response.error request_failed: "Integration root must be inside the workspace: apps/app"`; passing `integrations: []` returned a successful sessionId, so the bug is the default-built integration's cwd resolution on Windows.
